rules.title: Only ?Sized is a permitted relaxed bound
rules.statement: A relaxed bound `?Trait` on a type parameter is permitted only when Trait = Sized. `?Sized` clears the parameter's implicit Sized bound; any other `?Trait` is a hard error "relaxed bound '?T' is not permitted (only `?Sized` is supported)".

rules.title: Relaxed markers are consumed, never positive bounds
rules.statement: A relaxed `?Trait` marker is removed from a type parameter's bound set during finalization; it is never carried forward as a positive bound to monomorphization or bound-checking.

rules.title: Type parameters are implicitly Sized
rules.statement: Every type parameter carries an implicit `Sized` bound by default; it is cleared only by an explicit `?Sized` relaxed bound.

rules.title: Fn-family parenthesized bound syntax
rules.statement: The traits Fn, FnMut, FnOnce admit a parenthesized bound form `Fn(P1, ..., Pn) -> R`; the parenthesized list supplies the argument types and `-> R` the return type (both optional), distinct from the `<...>` type-argument list.
examples: fn call<F: FnOnce(i32, i32) -> bool>(f: F) {}

rules.title: Higher-ranked trait bound binders
rules.statement: A trait bound may carry a `for<'a, 'b, ...>` higher-ranked lifetime binder; the bound lifetime names are recorded on the bound.
examples: fn f<F: for<'a> Fn(&'a i32)>(f: F) {}

rules.title: Associated-type equality constraints in bounds
rules.statement: A trait bound may bind associated types by equality, `Trait<Assoc = Ty>`; each `Assoc = Ty` is recorded as an associated-type equality on the bound.

rules.title: Lifetime args in trait bounds are recorded but not dispatched on
rules.statement: A lifetime argument at a trait bound's type-argument position (e.g. `Foo<'a>`) is captured for record only; regions are not tracked structurally for bound dispatch.
rules.divergence: Logos does not track regions structurally for bound dispatch; lifetime bound-args carry no dispatch significance.

rules.title: Const generic parameters
rules.statement: A type parameter list may contain const parameters `const N: T`; each carries a const value-type T and may be marked variadic.

rules.title: Variadic type parameter must be last
rules.statement: A variadic type parameter `T...` must be the final entry in the type-parameter list; a non-final variadic param is an error "variadic type parameter must be last".
rules.divergence: Variadic type/const parameters are a Logos addition not present in Rust.

rules.title: Default type arguments
rules.statement: A type parameter may declare a default `<T = Default>` (or `<T: Bound = Default>`); the default type is recorded and substituted at use sites when the argument is omitted.

rules.title: Type-outlives bounds
rules.statement: A type parameter may carry type-outlives bounds `T: 'a (+ 'b)*`; the outlived lifetime names are recorded on the parameter.

rules.title: where-clause bounds merge into parameter bounds
rules.statement: Bounds from a `where T: Trait, U: Trait2` clause are merged onto the corresponding type parameters; an inline `<T, F: Bound>` and the equivalent `where`-clause form are semantically identical, and sibling type-params are in scope when resolving where-clause bound arguments.

rules.title: where-clause with concrete subject is an obligation, not a param
rules.statement: A `where <ConcreteType>: Trait` clause (subject names a known type, e.g. `where i32: Show`) is a trivially-checked obligation and does not introduce a new type parameter; only a genuinely-undeclared type-param name in a where clause is added as a parameter.

rules.title: where-clause projection subject is parsed but not enforced
rules.statement: A `where C::Item<T>: Bound` clause whose subject is an associated-type projection is accepted but not yet enforced (parse-and-skip).
rules.uncertainty: Statement reflects current parse-and-skip behavior; full projection-bound checking is noted as a separate unimplemented feature.

rules.title: Sibling type-params visible to bound argument resolution
rules.statement: When resolving a type-parameter's bound arguments, all sibling type-param names in the same list are in scope as type variables (so `where F: FnOnce(T, T) -> bool` resolves T).

rules.title: Inferred holes in let-annotation filled from RHS type
rules.statement: An `_` (inferred) hole in a let annotation is filled from the structurally-matching concrete RHS type (e.g. `let v: Vec<_> = vec![1]` binds as `Vec<i32>`); the annotation's concrete parts win, holes take the RHS side. Mismatched shapes leave the annotation unchanged. A bare `_` against an integer-literal RHS defaults to i32 and against a float-literal RHS to f64.

rules.title: A type contains an inferred hole transitively
rules.statement: A type is considered to contain an inferred hole if it is `_` or if any of its type arguments, tuple elements, element type, or pointee transitively contains one.

rules.title: The Never type is uninhabited
rules.statement: The Never type `!` is uninhabited.

rules.title: Enum inhabitedness
rules.statement: An enum is uninhabited iff it has zero variants, or every variant has at least one uninhabited payload type; it is inhabited as soon as one variant is constructable (all its payload types inhabited).

rules.title: Composite inhabitedness
rules.statement: A struct is uninhabited iff any field type is uninhabited; a tuple iff any element type is uninhabited; an array `[T; N]` iff N > 0 and T is uninhabited (zero-length arrays are always inhabited).

rules.title: References to uninhabited types are treated as inhabited
rules.statement: A reference or pointer to an uninhabited type is conservatively treated as inhabited (only value-carrying composites are marked uninhabited).
rules.divergence: Rust treats `&!` as uninhabited; Logos stays conservative and treats `&Never` as inhabited.

rules.title: Substitution resolves symbolic array sizes
rules.statement: Substituting an array type `[T; N]` whose size is a symbolic const-var N: if N maps to a concrete const value, the size becomes that value; if it maps to another ConstVar, the symbolic name is updated.

rules.title: Substitution canonicalizes unsized inner types under ptr/ref
rules.statement: When substitution yields an UnsizedSlice inside a `&`/`&mut`/`*const`/`*mut`, it canonicalizes to a slice type (fat pointer); an UnsizedDyn canonicalizes to a trait object. A safe reference drops per-instance lifetime info on the slice (Logos lifetime model is elision-based at this layer).

rules.title: Substitution forms DstRef for references to DST structs
rules.statement: Substituting a `&`/`&mut`/`*const`/`*mut` to an effective DST struct yields a wide DstRef (carrying the struct name, package, mutability, and type-args) — UNLESS the struct is `#[self_describing]`, in which case a raw pointer stays thin (8B), its tail length recoverable in-band at deref.

rules.title: Substitution preserves package qualification
rules.statement: Substituting a struct or enum type preserves its package qualification (pkg_name) on the result.

rules.title: Variadic-tuple pack expansion
rules.statement: A single-element tuple whose sole element is a pack type-var `(A...)` splices in the elements of the concrete tuple A maps to during substitution, yielding the full concrete tuple.
rules.divergence: Variadic tuples are a Logos addition not present in Rust.

rules.title: Substitution preserves Closure/FnItem/FnPtr kind and FnItem identity
rules.statement: Substituting a callable type preserves its kind (Closure vs FnItem vs FnPtr) and substitutes parameter and return types; a FnItem additionally preserves its identity (struct_name + type_args), substituting the type_args.

rules.title: Associated-type projection resolution during substitution
rules.statement: Substituting an associated-type projection `Base::Assoc` first substitutes Base; if Base becomes a concrete type, the projection resolves via the impl's `type Assoc = ...` (direct keyed lookup, then generic base-name lookup, then a blanket-impl whose bound is satisfied by the concrete type), substituting impl and GAT parameters; otherwise it remains a projection with substituted base, GAT args, and lifetime args.

rules.title: Projection on a still-typevar base reduces via a satisfied blanket impl
rules.statement: A projection `K::Assoc` where K remains a type-var reduces when K's recorded bounds include a trait for which a blanket `impl<DT: BoundTrait> Trait for DT` exists (with all extra bounds also among K's bounds); the result substitutes the blanket's target typevar with K (kept as a type-var).

rules.title: CTFE folds bare-ident const paths to their value
rules.statement: Compile-time const evaluation resolves a bare-identifier const path (e.g. inside `metacall { N }`) to its registered right-hand-side value.

rules.title: Reference-typed where-clause subject
rules.statement: A where-clause predicate's subject may be a reference type: `&T: Bound (+ Bound)*`, `&mut T: Bound (+ Bound)*`, or `for<'a> &'a T: Bound (+ Bound)*` (an associated-type subject `T::Item: Bound` is likewise accepted syntactically). Such a predicate is parsed as a TYPE_PARAM node carrying a TYPE field (the `&T`/`&mut T`/assoc-type node) instead of a NAME field, distinguishing it from the plain `T: Bound` form which falls through to the ordinary type_param rule. Sema's where-clause walker resolves the TYPE node; for a `&T`/`&mut T` subject over a type-param T, it records the listed bound(s) on the underlying type-param T, flagging each as `on_ref_subject` (with `is_ref_mut` set for `&mut`), so the method resolver applies these bounds only to a receiver of the matching (shared vs. mutable) reference kind. An associated-type projection subject is accepted and parsed but only parse-and-skipped semantically (not yet enforced); full projection-bound checking is a separate, unimplemented feature.
